title: EA.hy 926 RhoA Fret with PAsssr in Flow Cytometry
author: Cody Roberts
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfxujpnw
materials: Allow Cells to grow to 75%-95% confluence.

steps.title: Seed EA.hy 926 sensor cells
steps.instruction: Plate EA.hy 926 RhoA sensor cells into each well of a 6‑well plate at approximately 5 × 10⁵ cells per well (seeding density ~3 × 10⁵ cells, confluence ~1.2 × 10⁶ cells). Aim for 75‑95 % confluence the next day.

steps.title: Replace media with serum‑free VEGF
steps.instruction: On the morning of the experiment, aspirate existing media and add DMEM (serum‑free) supplemented with VEGF (use the same working concentration as in the referenced migration assay) and 0.1 % (mass/volume) BSA. VEGF stock is stored at –80 °C.

steps.title: Add treatment reagents
steps.instruction: Treat cells for 4–8 hours depending on the experimental condition:

substeps.instruction: RhoA inhibition well: add C3 at 1 µg ml⁻¹ (verify concentration).
CMG2 inhibition well: add PAsssr at 200 pM for final assay, but initially add 10 nM PAsssr to test for subtle effects. Unlabeled PAsssr is stored at –20 °C in a box labeled PA.

steps.title: Detach cells with trypsin
steps.instruction: After the treatment period, aspirate the media from each well and add 0.5 ml of Trypsin to each well.

steps.title: Incubate trypsinized cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates for 10 minutes (room temperature).

steps.title: Collect cells and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Transfer the trypsin‑cell suspension from each well into 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes and spin at 200 g, 24 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Wash cells with cold PBS
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant, then add 200 µl of pre‑chilled PBS to each tube. Pipet up and down to break up any clumped cells.

steps.title: Resuspend for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Transfer the 200 µl PBS‑cell suspension to a 96‑well plate, keep the plate on ice, and proceed to flow cytometry analysis.
